title: Ezekiel's Silent Grief
description: God tells the prophet Ezekiel that his wife, the delight of his eyes, will die suddenly, and he is forbidden to mourn publicly – no lamentation, no tears, no bread of mourning. When his wife dies in the evening, Ezekiel obeys the next morning. When the people ask what this means, he explains that it is a sign: God will desecrate the sanctuary and let their sons and daughters fall by the sword, and the people too will mourn in silence, wasting away in their sins. Ezekiel must remain silent until a fugitive arrives with news of Jerusalem’s fall – then his mouth will be opened as a sign to the people [ref:Ezekiel 24:15-27|Ezekiel 24:15-27].
